Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:5: And in the book Chassidim (section 14) it is written, at the root of love: in order to serve with joy, a person should take an example from flesh and blood - if he knew something to be the will of the king, he would not rest or be still until he fulfilled the king's will, though he is a maggot and a worm like himself; and he would rejoice greatly that his deeds came before the king, to his will. How much more so, for the will of the Creator, who lives and endures, must one exert himself and seek how to do and fulfill the will of His commandment - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:6: And further, he should think and say in his heart: behold, all the host of heaven perform their service with joy, glad and rejoicing to do the will of their Owner, and their supernal service is doubly greater than our own - for the spheres never rest from their motion, and so the sun forever revolves, and every morning when it goes forth, it goes forth with joy, as it is said (Psalms 19:6), "it rejoices like a mighty man" - and it sings before the Omnipresent, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained, that they say the psalm "Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name" (Psalms 105). And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 196a), in these words: at the hour the sun rises in its sphere, it opens with a pleasant voice and utters song - what does it say? "Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name," and so on, "sing to Him a new song," and so on; and Israel praise the Holy One, blessed be He, by day with the sun, this is what is written (Psalms 72:5), "they shall fear You as long as the sun endures." And although we have already established this verse [elsewhere], Rabbi Elazar said: were it not that the people of the world are dull of heart and their eyes sealed, they could not withstand all the sweetness of the sun's sphere when it rises - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:7: And further, they said in Midrash Tanchuma (Achrei, 9): this is what Scripture says (Psalms 113:3), "from the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is praised" - from the hour the sun rises until it sets, it gives praise to the Holy One, blessed be He. And so you find, at the hour Joshua stood at Gibeon and wished to silence it, it does not say "sun, stand still at Gibeon," but "sun, be silent at Gibeon" - for at every hour it moves, it gives praise to the Holy One, blessed be He, and at every hour it praises, it has (variant: does not have) the strength to stand still - therefore Joshua said to it, "be silent" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:8: And one who heard and saw testified to me about men who went to the land of India to see the place where the sun rises and sets - two went, and one returned mute. The one who drew very close to hear the melody of the sun's voice died, and the other became mute; and this one, upon his return, said this by writing. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Sanhedrin, concerning Sennacherib, that he made them hear the sound of the sun's sphere.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:9: And along the lines that the sun sings, the supernal beings too sing and praise the Cause of all causes - whether among the emanated, the created, the formed, or the made - for everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He created only for His glory, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7), "everyone that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him" - and glory is praise and lauding, along the lines of (Psalms 29:9), "and in His temple all say, Glory." And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Midrash Tehillim (Psalm 19), in these words: "the heavens declare" - this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 16:4), "the LORD has made everything for His own purpose [la-ma'anehu]" - for His praise [le-killuso], as it says (Psalms 147:7), "sing to the LORD with thanksgiving." Another interpretation: for His testimony, and so on. And he further says: another interpretation, "the LORD has made everything for His praise" - for everything praises Him for His works and His deeds, and all His works praise Him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:10: And to this King David, peace be upon him, referred in the psalm (ibid. 148:1), "praise the LORD from the heavens," and so on, "praise Him all His angels, praise Him all His hosts, praise Him sun and moon." And he explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pekudei, page 232a), in these words: Halleluyah, "praise the LORD from the heavens" - this is the beginning of the six directions to spread downward, for this is the secret of what stands to be asked, as it says, "for ask now of the former days that were before you," and so on (Deuteronomy 4:32) - up to here there is permission to ask, from here on there is no standing to ask, because it is a hidden and concealed place. And therefore, "praise the LORD from the heavens, praise Him in the heights" - these are the two sides that are the height of the beginning, right and left, and from here all the others spread downward in the secret of the ranks, to be properly arranged. "Praise Him, all His angels" - these are the two pillars that stand beneath the body, to support the body upon them; come and see, those pillars upon which the body leans stand here in the secret of angels, because they need to be sent from place to place, and from this secret emerge those called angels, who are sent to go on their Master's errand from place to place. "Praise Him, all His hosts" - this is the place from which all the supernal holy hosts emerge, the secret of the holy sign, which is marked upon all the other myriads, as it says, "the LORD of Hosts is His name" - it is a sign among all the other hosts and myriads. "Praise Him, sun and moon" - in it stands this secret, and it is the sun that gives light, and in it stand the supernal stars that shine, and the constellations - and this has already been established. Afterward it returns above to that place that stands at the height of heights, and there is the anchoring of all. Afterward, "praise the LORD from the earth" - corresponding to these, "fire and hail" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:11: And his intent is that "praise the LORD from the heavens" refers, in general, to the six extremities; "praise Him in the heights" - Chesed and Gevurah; "praise Him, all His angels" - Netzach and Hod, and as to why he called them angels, he said the reason is that angels are those sent from place to place, and their source is from the supernal thighs; "praise Him, all His hosts" - corresponding to Yesod; "praise Him, sun and moon" - corresponding to Tiferet and Malchut; "praise Him, highest heavens, and the waters that are above the heavens" - these are the three first [sefirot]. And afterward it descends below to the physical elements: "praise the LORD from the earth" - "sea monsters and all depths, fire and hail."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:12: And it is no wonder that he did not mention the praise of the created and formed beings [nivra'im, notzarim], for they were already mentioned in the praise "praise Him all His angels, praise Him all His hosts" - and though it would have been fitting to mention "His hosts" and afterward "His angels," it was necessitated by the order of the attributes. Behold, all existing things [are thus included].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:13: And all the more so what is below them - for all of them give song and praise to the Cause of causes, for even the Keter, "at the height of heights, the anchoring of all," of it is said "praise Him, highest heavens" - and afterward Scripture says, "let them praise the name of the LORD, for He commanded and they were created" - and this Name YHVH, we are compelled to say, is the first Name attached to the Cause of causes, who is "great and ruling," and so on, as explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1. And the praise and lauding is for having brought them into being and created them from nothing into something - and this is "for He commanded and they were created." And also in Keter this matter is fitting, for it too is emanated, though not in the language of command - and therefore you will find the shofar-mark [inverted trope] on the word "ki" [for], and a "tarcha" mark on the word "hu" [He] - understand this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:14: And it is found in the books of the opponents that above there is one minister, seated on a throne, who has a thousand mouths, and in each mouth a thousand tongues, and with each and every tongue he gives songs of joy and praises to his Owner - and he is called Yo-a-achtzatzbiron; and this minister is explained in the Tikkunim (beginning of page 135) as to his virtue - see there. And so, in the book Brit Menuchah, he explained several supernal ministers whose names end in "hon" and "ron" - the reason being that they are appointed over song, joy, and praise, and these are called "alamot shir" (Psalms 46:1), maidens appointed over song.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:15: And concerning this the men of the Great Assembly instituted for us (the Nishmat prayer): "were our mouth as full of song as the sea, and our tongue of joyous singing as its multitude of waves," and so on. And the meaning is that the supernal sea sings song, as he says (Psalms 30:13), "so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent," and along the lines of (ibid. 83:2), "O God, do not be silent" - for she forever arouses song to unify Abba and Imma, as my teacher explained in the Gate of Essence and Conduct (chapter 20); and "its waves" are the spirits of the throne within it, who also arouse song.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:16: And through this may be understood what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 69b) on the verse (Psalms 89:10), "when its waves rise, You still them" - in these words: "You still them" [teshabecham] literally means "praise" [shevach] is theirs, because they rise in desire to see; from here, whoever longs to gaze and to know, even though he cannot, praise is his, and everything praises him - to this point. And the meaning is that the supernal spirits of the throne go and run and lift themselves up in order to see and grasp with the supernal light that which is above their grasp; and even though they turn back, unable to grasp what is above their level, nonetheless it is praise for them that they have the desire to grasp more and to cleave to the supernal light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:17: And so too souls, after their passing, give thanks and praise to the Holy One, blessed be He, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 142a), in these words: this soul [nefesh], at the time the spirit [ru'ach] descends from the supernal light to dwell in the Garden of Eden, shines and glistens - it, while standing in the grave, is clothed in the image it had within the body originally, and all those bones, in that image of theirs, praise and give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He - this is what is written (Psalms 35:10), "all my bones shall say, LORD, who is like You" - it does not say "say" [omrot] but "shall say" [tomarnah]; and were permission given to the eye to see, on the night the Sabbath departs, and on the nights of the New Moon and festivals, [it would see] figures upon the graves giving thanks and praising the Holy One, blessed be He - but the foolishness of people prevents [this], and so on - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:18: And since all the supernal beings arouse song because of their desire to cleave to Him, correspondingly a person too must arouse song and praise to gladden his Owner, and in order to cleave to his Owner - for song causes cleaving. And this is when he remembers the abundance of His goodness and kindness upon him, as we say: "were our mouth as full of song as the sea... we would not suffice to thank You for one of the thousand thousands of thousands of miracles and wonders You performed for us and for our fathers, and the spirit and soul You breathed into our nostrils, and the tongue You placed in our mouths - behold, they shall thank and bless and sing praise to Your Name, our King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:19: And to this King David, peace be upon him, referred in saying (Psalms 31:8), "I will be glad and rejoice in Your kindness, for You have seen my affliction" - behold, joy is from the side of the kindness He has done him. And from this aspect David was forever a singer, and he commanded us to arouse song and joyous singing, saying (ibid. 33:1), "sing joyously, O righteous, in the LORD," "sing to Him a new song" (ibid. 33:3).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:20: And so you find that when a miracle was performed for Israel, they would immediately say song: "then Israel sang" (Exodus 15:1), "and Deborah sang" (Judges 5:1). And it is impossible for a miracle to occur without the attribute of Chesed participating in it - and so he explained in Parashat Vayikra (page 8a) on the verse (Psalms 100:2), "serve the LORD with joy," that joy comes from the side of the Kohen, in these words: joy is established through the priest, because he is always distant from judgment, and the priest must always be found with a shining, joyful countenance, more joyful than the whole people - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:21: And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 8b) they asked concerning the verse "serve the LORD with joy," and so on: one who has sinned and transgressed a negative commandment of the Torah, his remedy is to bring a sacrifice, confess, and grieve - and if he weeps, all the better for him - if so, where is his joy and joyous song? And they answered: at the time the Temple stood, this matter depended on the priest and the Levite - for the priest, the man of kindness, is the master of joy, and the Levite sings - behold, joy and joyous song. And afterward they asked, of blessed memory: now that there is no sacrifice, one who sins before his Master and returns to Him - certainly with bitterness of soul, in sadness, in weeping, with a broken spirit - how can joy and joyous song be established, since they are not found with him? Rather, they have already established that the praises of his Master and the joy of Torah and the joyous song of Torah - this is joy and joyous song.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:22: And further he gave another explanation there: that "joy" [simchah] and "joyous song" [rinnah] are Yesod and Malchut - and the intent is that his intention should be to unify these attributes, concerning which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 8a), one should always enter [a synagogue] the space of two doorways - and further, they elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 165a) resolving this question - see there. And behold, according to this, the general nature of the joy shall be that the Name has granted him to be among His servants who unify Him, which not every person merits.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:23: And according to the plain sense, the joy a person should arouse in his prayer, especially if it is in the synagogue or the study hall, lies in the very existence of prayer - for prayer is a supernal need, and the proof is that from it a crown is made for the King of the world; and it is fitting for a person to say in his heart: from where have I merited to give a crown to the King of the world? Rather, the King, in His abundant kindness, drew me near to Him - and therefore it is fitting that I perform His service with joy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:24: Also in the very existence of prayer - what Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Zohar, Parashat Terumah, page 131b): that three camps of angels stand in the synagogue for the repair of prayer. One camp is those angels who say song with Israel by day, and these arrange all the hymns, because there is another band who say song at night, and these do not stand with Israel by day. The second camp are those who stand at every single sanctification [kedushah] that Israel sanctify below, and he said, and in their dominion are all those aroused in all those firmaments during that prayer of Israel. The third camp are the seven maidens fit to be given to her - these are the seven supernal chambers arranged in the Yotzer prayer [Shacharit blessings]. And he said, and all of them are arranged through the arrangement of Israel, which is arranged below - namely the songs and praises, and through that prayer which Israel pray - to this point. Behold, all the repair of the supernal camps and the repair of the Shechinah with her camps depends on the prayer of Israel. And so they said further on (ibid. page 132), that there is no sanctification above except if there is sanctification below, as it is said (Leviticus 22:32), "and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel" - and the rest of his words we have copied in the Gate of Holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:25: And when standing in the synagogue, one should be joyful that he stands in the House of the LORD, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 122:1), "I was glad when they said to me, let us go to the House of the LORD," and it says (ibid. 84:3), "my soul longs, indeed it yearns, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:26: And in occupation with Torah, one should be joyful, as they said (Berachot, chapter 4, mishnah 2): Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah would pray upon entering the study hall and upon leaving it, and said, "and upon my leaving, I give thanks for my portion" - and they explained in the Gemara (cf. Berachot 28b) that he would say, "we give thanks before You, LORD our God, that You have set our portion among those who sit in the study hall," and so on, "I run to the life of the World to Come" - and in its place we shall elaborate on its explanation, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:27: And further our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 117a), concerning Elisha, of whom it is said (2 Kings 3:15), "and now bring me a minstrel," and so on, "and the hand of the LORD came upon him" - this teaches that the Shechinah rests neither out of laziness, nor out of sadness, nor out of laughter, nor out of levity, nor out of idle talk and vain words, but out of the joy of a commandment, as it is said, "and now bring me a minstrel," and so on. Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rav: and so too for a matter of halachah. Rav said: and so too for a good dream. Is that so, and so on - until he sits in awe and opens with the teaching.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:28: In occupation with the commandments, one should be joyful, for the commandments are the King's jewels, and He adorns Himself with them - it is fitting to be joyful, especially when one knows what repair the performance of that commandment effects and what benefit it brings his soul; then he will be all the more joyful, and in the Gate of Commandments we shall elaborate further. Concerning this it is said (Psalms 19:9), "the precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:29: And especially in the matter of charity, one must be joyful in giving it, for through it he cleaves to the Shechinah, as it is said (ibid. 17:15), "I, in righteousness, shall behold Your face," as we shall elaborate in its place. Do you not see that King David, peace be upon him, and Israel, when they donated for the building of the Temple, did so with joy, as it is said (1 Chronicles 29:9), "and the people rejoiced at their offering willingly, for with a whole heart they offered willingly to the LORD," and King David also rejoiced greatly - it follows that a commandment performed with a good heart itself gives joy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:30: And in receiving every person with a pleasant countenance there is a secret, as explained in the Idra (Idra, Parashat Naso, page 133a), in these words: we have learned, what is written (Isaiah 61:10), "I will greatly rejoice in the LORD" - it is said of the Ancient of Days, that this is the joy of all - to this point. And further on he says that from the two supernal faces of the Ancient Ones, the face of Ze'ir Anpin shines below - and concerning the supernal faces it is said (Proverbs 16:15), "in the light of the king's countenance is life." And afterward he says, we have learned: when these two "apples" are revealed, Ze'ir Anpin appears with joy, and all those lamps below shine, and all worlds rejoice and are complete with all completeness, and all rejoice and shine, and all goodness never ceases - to this point, relevant here. Behold, all realities need joy, for in all the worlds they are aroused from the supernal faces - and behold, when a person receives every person with a pleasant countenance and a shining face, this indicates the face of Ze'ir Anpin that shone from the supernal faces, and this is the supernal completeness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:31: All the more so if one receives the presence of a sage or his teacher - for receiving his presence is like receiving the presence of the Shechinah (Yerushalmi Eruvin, chapter 5, halachah 1) - it must be with joy. Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Tanchuma (Shemot 27) concerning Aaron, of whom it is said (Exodus 4:14), "and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart" - it does not say simply "glad," but "glad in his heart"; Rashbi said: the heart that rejoiced in his brother's greatness shall wear the Urim and Tummim, as it is said, "and you shall put in the breastplate of judgment," and so on, "and they shall be upon Aaron's heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:32: The joy of festivals - it is already known what they explained (Pesachim 109a), that on a festival a person is obligated to rejoice with meat and wine, he and his household, and so on. And the reason the festival is called "ushpiza" [a guest] is that it comes from time to time, and just as a guest must be received with a pleasant countenance, so must the festivals be received - and the reason is that on festivals a new light is revealed, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Emor concerning the holy convocations.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:33: And in the Tikkunim (page 58b) he said, in these words: and further, the Shechinah is called "festival" [chag] at every appointed time and festival - the festival of the three pilgrimage feasts, of which it is said (Exodus 23:14), "three times you shall hold a feast to Me in the year," and for her sake "all your males shall appear," to fulfill "remember" and "observe" - "remember" for the male, "observe" for the female. All those who go to gaze upon the Shechinah must give her a gift, this is what is written (Deuteronomy 16:16), "and he shall not appear before the LORD empty-handed," and must rejoice in her, this is what is written (ibid. 16:14), "and you shall rejoice in your feast," for she is called the joy of the Holy One, blessed be He; and whoever goes to see her must guard himself from sadness, which is Lilith, darkness, the sadness of the spleen (variant: of Sheol), which is a blemish, of which it is said (Leviticus 21:18), "any man who has a blemish shall not approach" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:34: And especially on the festival of Sukkot, called "the time of our joy," as we say in our prayers, one should be joyful, especially while in the sukkah, as it is said in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, end of page 103), in these words: a person must rejoice every single day with a shining countenance with these guests who dwell with him. And my teacher, peace be upon him, was precise concerning his saying "every single day," and not saying, in general, "these seven days" - to show that on each and every day one must have a joy of its own, for the seven days are the seven guests [ushpizin], so on each day he has his own guest and must show him joy. And he further says on: like Rav Hamnuna, who, when he entered the sukkah, would rejoice - and the rest of his words need not be copied, up to "and with all this, one must gladden the poor, for the portion of these destined guests is [given to] the poor" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:35: And among the conditions of the joy of the festivals is that one not rejoice with frivolity and outings after the manner of the joy of the gentiles in their festivals, as it is said (Hosea 9:1), "do not rejoice, O Israel, to exultation, like the peoples" - rather, the joy should be in the festival itself, in the days of holy convocation, as explained above; and it is like a person standing in darkness who rejoices when a new light comes to him - so one must rejoice in the joy of Torah on the festival more than at other times, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Yerushalmi Shabbat, chapter 15, halachah 3), that festivals were given to Israel only to occupy themselves with Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:36: And know that the reality of joy causes unification, for it is impossible for the caused to draw near to the cause unless there be joy between them, that the cause desire its caused to draw near it, and likewise the joy of the caused to be included in its cause, in order to be illumined by it - and this is "an offering to the LORD," as explained in the Tikkunim (page 34b), where they say, in these words: and when they offer, father joins with mother, son with daughter, each with his mate - the supernal heh toward the yud, the lower heh toward the vav - this is the offering that goes up and down, at that time (Ezekiel 37:7), "and the bones drew near, bone to its bone." And at the end of his words: and when it descends to the son, it is said of it (Leviticus 6:5), "and the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it" - kindled with the flames of love - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:37: And "the flames of love" are joy itself, and it is the fire that comes from the side of the left, which is the wine that gladdens, and it is what causes the union - and so he explained in the Zohar (Parashat Korach, page 178b) concerning "and the Levite shall serve, he" (Numbers 18:23), in these words: "he" [hu] - he completes the completeness so that all becomes one. "He" - it is simple, to receive the Community of Israel, as it says (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," in order to join the union together - who arouses the love? You must say, "Hu-A" [these letters] - to this point. And there he gives several interpretations of the word "hu-a," and according to this interpretation, "hu-a" is in Binah, and from there the joy of the Community of Israel is aroused in the union, in such a way that the Atzilut is unified in its entire completeness as one. It follows that the essence of joy is the unification and binding of the whole of Atzilut as one, and its illumination through the Emanator - for this is the whole of joy, that they all shine and unify as one, until the Emanator shines within them properly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:38: And with this introduction we shall understand what the Psalmist, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 32:11), "be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous," and so too (ibid. 35:9), "and my soul shall rejoice in the LORD" - for the essence of the soul's joy is in its shining with the light of the whole of Atzilut, included in YHVH, as is known. And if we wish to explain that the Name YHVH here refers, without further specification, to Tiferet, this too is fitting, because then it draws supernal life from Him who gives life to all existing things, who is bound to this Name, and all is one - for Tiferet includes the ten [sefirot] within the Name YHVH that is in it, and it is the light of colors, as I have elaborated in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:39: And therefore whoever wishes to gladden his soul should seclude himself part of the day to contemplate the greatness of the letters of YHVH, as we explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 5. And proof of this is what King David, peace be upon him, said (ibid. 16:8-9), "I have set the LORD always before me... therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoices" - and "my glory" is the soul, and because the soul's emanation is from the Name YHVH, as he says (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God," therefore, when he contemplates the Name YHVH, the soul shines and is polished with a wondrous polish, and this is joy - and from the power of that illumination it has the power to give some sparkle even to the flesh, such that "my flesh too shall dwell securely," so that the worm shall not rule over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:40: And this is the virtue of the righteous who cleave to the Name of the LORD, that even in their death they are called living - for because of their cleaving to the Name YHVH, which is the source of life, they impart some vitality even to the flesh, such that they are called living even in their death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:41: And it is possible to explain "my heart is glad" as corresponding to the flesh, and "my glory" as corresponding to the inwardness within it - and this and that are both created through the Name YHVH, as explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7. And therefore, after death, it is not only that the soul is bound to the root to which it was cleaved in life, so that even now it dwells securely - but even the flesh, since the flesh too was cleaved and rejoiced in YHVH, and the heart is the essence of all 248 limbs - it is fitting that the worm not rule over any of the flesh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:42: And behold, through this we shall understand his saying (Psalms 33:1), "sing joyously, O righteous, ba-Hashem [in the LORD]" - for it would have been fitting to say "sing joyously, O righteous, to the LORD," along the lines of (ibid. 105:2), "sing to Him, make music to Him," and it does not say "sing in Him." Rather, the matter may be explained in two ways: the first, that it is along the lines of saying "the righteous in YHVH" - meaning, and so now he commands the righteous, that when they sing joyously, their intent should be to unify the Name YHVH, and this is "ba-Hashem" - that this Name be before you, that you unify it - so that such joyous song is complete cleaving.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:43: And it is possible to say that the intent is that joyous song in general causes cleaving. How so? Because in a person's recounting the praises of the King of the world - along the lines of King David's praises, peace be upon him, and likewise the several praises of the Omnipresent composed by the pious Rabbi Yehuda HaLevi, peace be upon him - reciting them causes his soul's cleaving to his God, for the Holy One, blessed be He, desires that His greatness and glory be recounted, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 145:4), "one generation shall praise Your works to another," and so on, "the glorious splendor of Your majesty... I will speak" - and most of the psalm speaks of this, that it is fitting to recount His praises, His glory, and His greatness, and the like - and all these songs arouse desire and love between Israel and their Father in Heaven. And the parable for this is a king of flesh and blood, who, when he hears that a servant of his servants recounts his praises and his glory, certainly the king will love him - for the king says, certainly this one who recounts my praises certainly loves me, and it is fitting that I too love him - and the parallel is understood. And this is what he said, "sing joyously, O righteous" - when you sing joyously, O righteous, immediately you are cleaved to YHVH. And there is support for this from the division of the cantillation marks, that on the word "tzaddikim" there is a "tarcha" mark. And as they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13, page 23b), that the song itself contains an allusion to YHVH, in these words: ten spheres (variant: strings) are the yud, corresponding to the ten fingers that strike in melody, five against five, and these are heh-heh that ascend into the yud, in the six ranks that are the vav, in which they ascend and descend - to this point. And further on: when the daughter ascends in song, the eagle takes the yud in its mouth and upon its head, the vav in its body, the heh-heh in its wings - Adam: yud-vav-dalet, heh-alef, vav-alef-vav, dalet-alef, riding upon all - to this point. And through this may be understood "ba-Hashem" - the intent being that the joyous song itself should be in YHVH, as alluded.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:44: And further, it is possible [to explain] "ba-Hashem" by what we have explained several times, that the Name YHVH is imprinted in man in every single limb, and even in his spirit - so the instruments of song in his mouth are [themselves] YHVH, and through them he sings - and this is (Psalms 35:10), "all my bones shall say, LORD, who is like You."
